final_report: delivered in-conversation at Gate 4 (harness policy: orchestrator returns findings as text, not a report file)

findings.title: The cheap tier cost MORE in absolute terms than the premium tier
findings.explanation: Sonnet was 2.4x cheaper per output token, exactly as intended, but mechanical work emitted 3.3x more output. A 2.4x rate advantage loses to a 3.3x volume disadvantage and the totals invert. Routing was correct throughout (rule 7 codegen, rule 8 tests, rules 0/6 judgment).
findings.implication: A mixed policy pays off on input-heavy / output-light phases (review, analysis, planning) and pays off LEAST on test generation - which is exactly where cheap tiers are usually assumed to shine. Tuning options: batch test packets far more coarsely, or accept that the tests phase prices like premium work regardless of tier.

findings.scope: plugin-wide (every claude-cli policy, not just this run)
findings.title: budget.maxOutputTokens is INERT on adapter claude-cli
findings.explanation: ClaudeCliAdapter spawns the CLI without any max-tokens flag, so budget.maxOutputTokens is recorded in telemetry but never constrains the model.
findings.consequence: Budgets on claude-cli leaves are documentation, not control, and the ceiling-doubling retry described in the pipeline skill (hit_output_cap / retry_reason: output_cap) can never trigger on this adapter. Cost cannot be bounded per-packet on claude-cli.
findings.affects: every policy whose leaves use adapter: claude-cli

findings.title: pnpm --filter @kaneo/api db:generate emits 2-space JSON into a tab-formatted repo and reddens biome ci

evidence.ci_job: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `pnpm exec biome ci .` as the FIRST job

findings.root_cause: drizzle-kit writes meta/_journal.json and meta/<n>_snapshot.json with 2-space indent; biome.json sets formatter.indentStyle=tab and the javascript override does not apply to JSON; apps/api/drizzle/** is not excluded from Biome file discovery.
findings.why_missed: The run linted the 18 files it EDITED, not the files a generator WROTE. The four-command verification gate contains no linter at all.
findings.superseded_advice: Security review F-3 proposed the OPPOSITE fix (regenerate via db:generate so formatting matches). That is backwards - db:generate is what produces the spaces. Recorded as superseded.

findings.title: apps/docs/openapi.json is 11 route-groups stale and CI has no spec-freshness check

evidence.regeneration_diff: 1481 insertions / 166 deletions, of which exactly 2 lines were wipLimit

findings.decision: Allowlist was extended at Gate 3 and the spec WAS regenerated, then REVERTED byte-for-byte (md5 c125cebe51982a8b5e0d97083840ef04 restored, path git-clean). Shipping it would bury a 2-line contract change in ~1300 lines of unrelated drift, violate AGENTS.md on not mixing unrelated cleanup, and make this benchmark arm diff-incomparable with the other three arms.
findings.follow_up: Dedicated ticket: regenerate apps/docs/openapi.json on its own so the drift is reviewable; add a spec-freshness check to CI. The ABSENCE of that check is why an 11-route gap went unnoticed.

findings.title: A discovery-phase claim was falsified by security review
findings.evidence: discovery.md asserted get-public-project.ts "does not build a columns projection, so the public path is unaffected". The controller is three lines and delegates straight to getTasks(id), inheriting the column projection wholesale.
findings.consequence: wipLimit is served anonymously via GET /api/public-project/:id. Accepted as intended at Gate 3 (see F-1 disclosure decision). Had no reviewer traced it, the run would have shipped believing the public surface was untouched.
findings.lesson: A discovery-phase assertion that a code path is UNAFFECTED is a claim that must be re-verified downstream, not inherited.

findings.title: 300s hard timeout kills long single-shot generations with no partial result

evidence.recovery: split into tp_plan_002a / tp_plan_002b, which returned in 59s and 87s

findings.guidance: Cap any single claude-cli dispatch at roughly 5000 output tokens.

disclosure_decisions.status: ACCEPTED as intended, closed at Gate 3
disclosure_decisions.title: wipLimit is served anonymously via GET /api/public-project/:id
disclosure_decisions.reasoning: An anonymous viewer of a public project already sees every task in the column and therefore already sees the count. The limit adds only the team internal target. Excluding it would require forking or post-processing the shared board projection for marginal benefit.
disclosure_decisions.revisit_if: public boards ever stop exposing task lists

telemetry_integrity.estimated_detail: plan_task_packets ($0.0850) was handled in-session on the same Opus tier the policy names for that phase, because decomposition depends on exact working-tree file contents a freshly spawned claude -p worker cannot see, and the 300s timeout risk was already demonstrated. Tokens are char/3.8 estimates priced from the policy pricing block. Flagged so it is not mistaken for vendor-measured.
